subject: Renewal: adaptive commit hedging and spike-buffer proposal
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: adaptive commit hedging and spike-buffer proposal

Hi Elena —

Congrats again on hitting the Q2 latency targets in production — great to see BrightPath getting more predictable tail latency. With renewal coming up, I wanted to propose a structure that lets you keep unit economics tight while protecting against short-term, high-impact spikes during marketing/feature launches. High level:

- Reserve baseline commit that maps to your steady-state 95th-percentile GPU utilization.
- Add a small, billed "hedge buffer" (flex slab) that can be used for short-lived spikes and is convertible to committed capacity if sustained.
- Canary burst pool for critical windows (24–72h) with explicit triggers and auto-fallbacks.

Attached is a draft addendum (redwood-commit-hedge-addendum-v2.pdf) and a short spike-mitigation playbook we use with other customers. Key numbers I suggest based on your last six weeks: baseline: 42 NVIDIA-A100 equivalents committed, hedge buffer: +8 GPUs available as burst, canary pool: +4 GPUs per region. Pricing uses blended reserve + short-burst rate; conversion to committed capacity would follow a 60-day utilization sustained rule.

If this looks reasonable, next steps:
1) confirm target baseline (I used 42 as above).
2) pick preferred burst/hedge conversion window (30/60/90 days) — default is 60.
3) agree on canary trigger criteria (we can propose thresholds).

Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week to walk through the playbook and show the utilization histogram.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | (415) 555-0186

Attachments: redwood-commit-hedge-addendum-v2.pdf (PDF), spike-mitigation-playbook.pdf (PDF)

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightpath.ai>

Thanks Marcus — this is useful. A few quick clarifying questions before we take the attached addendum to procurement: 

1) How do you measure "sustained" utilization for conversion? We had some transient bursts from a marketing campaign in July that looked like sustained for ~14 days.
2) Can the hedge buffer be regional (we run EU/US split) and billed separately?
3) Any impact on SLA/priority routing when the canary pool is in use?

Also Craig wants a line that says we can opt out of conversion within the first renewal quarter without penalty (he's wary of being locked in). Can you and legal weigh in?

Elena
Director of Platform Ops | BrightPath AI
elena.morales@brightpath.ai

Subject: Re: Renewal: adaptive commit hedging and spike-buffer proposal (internal)

Marcus / Vanessa —

Quick internal run of the numbers against BrightPath's last 90 days of telemetry:
- Steady-state 95th pctl maps to ~39–44 A100-equivalent GPUs depending on sequence-length distribution. 42 is a conservative baseline.
- The July marketing burst you mention spiked for 12–16 days but only breached 80% utilization for the baseline for 9 of those days; it qualifies as a "short surge."
- If we offer a 60-day sustained-utilization conversion rule, the example you share would not auto-convert. If they want a 30-day conversion threshold we should price the hedge buffer ~8–12% higher.

Recommendations:
1) Offer regionally scoped hedge buffers (US/EU) with independent conversion clocks — gives BrightPath control and reduces their procurement friction.
2) Canary pool should carry preemptive routing lower than committed capacity but above best-effort; this keeps SLAs intact for committed traffic.
3) For the opt-out ask: we can include a 90-day no-conversion grace for the first renewal quarter, but it needs approval from Pricing and Legal — that delays signature by ~3 business days.

Vanessa — can you confirm whether we have spare burst capacity in IAD for August? If not, we can map to our multi-region burst pool.

-Karthik
Director, Dedicated Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Subject: Renewal: updated addendum + regional hedge option

Elena —

Thanks for the questions. Per our internal sync (thread below) we've updated the addendum to be region-specific and added an explicit "first-renewal grace" clause you requested. Summary of changes in redwood-commit-hedge-addendum-v2.pdf:

- Regionally scoped hedge buffers: US (8 GPUs) / EU (4 GPUs) with independent 60-day conversion clocks (customer can request 30-day for higher rate).
- Clarified conversion measurement: rolling-window, customer-level 95th-percentile of per-GPU utilization measured across 72h sampling intervals (we can export the metric feed).
- Canary pool routing priority: committed > canary > best-effort; no change to SLA for committed traffic when canary is active.
- First-renewal grace: BrightPath may opt-out of converting any hedge buffers for up to 90 days after renewal signature without penalty.

I've attached the revised addendum and the spike playbook. If this version looks ok to you I can route to Legal for a quick redline and procurement for countersign. Proposed next step: 30-min review on Wed 8/14 10:00 PDT — does that work?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
